>Revolution is about providing a better system and more consistent worldview. 

Yes, the revolutions of the past have mainly been ALL about that.... Promising an unattainable Utopia, and then shitting all over their own ideas just to attain this or that short-term goal. Look how far they got; they are all guilty of this. 

From ISAIF (quoting the paragraph in full, but it is the last two sentences that really drive the point home): 

182. It will be objected that the French and Russian Revolutions were failures. But most revolutions have two goals. One is to destroy an old form of society and the other is to set up the new form of society envisioned by the revolutionaries. The French and Russian revolutionaries failed (fortunately!) to create the new kind of society of which they dreamed, but they were quite successful in destroying the old society. We have no illusions about the feasibility of creating a new, ideal form of society. Our goal is only to destroy the existing form of society. 

>If we don't define our ideas growth and the fanaticism needed to commit become impossible
Ted speaks brilliantly and very clearly about this in chapters 3 and 4 of ATRev. If you haven't done so already, take a good look at those two chapters.
